mission.label: Our Mission
mission.paragraph1: AntangPatahu Mahaga Lewu (AMAL) is a foundation that serves as a strategic partner of Social Forestry in Central Kalimantan. We facilitate Carbon Projects from mineral forests and peatlands, support the development of Non-Timber Forest Product (NTFP) businesses, and provide API Licences for ESG needs of strategic partners.
mission.paragraph2: With a focus on carbon projects, non-timber forest product utilization, and strategic partnerships, we assist communities in 4 districts of Central Kalimantan with a strong commitment to environmental conservation and community welfare.
mission.paragraph3: We believe that community welfare and forest conservation are two inseparable sides of the same coin — both must go hand in hand to achieve truly sustainable development.

karbon.heroDescription: Carbon projects in mineral forests and peatlands are the most cost-effective nature-based climate change mitigation instruments (Nature-Based Solutions / NbS) at the global level. Indonesia's tropical ecosystems — particularly in Central Kalimantan — hold highly strategic carbon reserves: tropical peatlands can store up to 2,000–3,000 tons CO₂e/ha, while tropical mineral forests store an average of 150–400 tons CO₂e/ha of above- and below-ground biomass.

karbon.duaEkosistemDesc: Mineral forests and peatlands — two ecosystems with distinctly different characteristics and carbon management strategies
karbon.eco1Desc: Mineral forests store carbon primarily in above-ground biomass (AGB) and below-ground biomass (BGB), with limited contribution from mineral soil carbon. Protection of forest cover is the absolute priority.
karbon.eco1WilayahDominan: Gunung Mas (montane forest, upstream Barito and Kahayan watersheds) and parts of Kapuas (mineral zones outside the peat dome)
karbon.eco2Desc: Tropical peatland ecosystems store carbon reserves far exceeding those of mineral forests, mostly below ground in peat layers that can reach depths of 10–15 meters. Hydrological disturbance is the primary trigger of peat emissions.
karbon.eco2WilayahDominan: Katingan (deep peat dome, Katingan Mentaya benchmark), Pulang Pisau (former PLG, intensive BRGM restoration), parts of Kapuas (transitional and coastal peatlands of the watershed)
karbon.benchmarkKatingan: Katingan Mentaya Project Benchmark: As the world's largest peatland carbon project (120,000+ ha), producing >7.5 million VCUs/year with average soil carbon content of >2,400 tons CO₂e/ha. The YAMAL project operates within the same landscape context.
karbon.metodologiDesc: International standards and methodologies used in YAMAL carbon projects
karbon.method1App: Prevention of deforestation & degradation of mineral forests (REDD+)
karbon.kegiatanMitigasiDesc: Emission reduction and carbon sequestration enhancement through 11 integrated mitigation activities
karbon.mitigasi1Deskripsi: Protection of forest areas from land conversion, illegal logging, and encroachment to maintain carbon stocks stored in biomass and soil. Includes boundary enforcement, routine patrols, and tenure conflict resolution.
karbon.mitigasi2Deskripsi: Restoration of critical areas through revegetation, replanting of local species, watershed rehabilitation, and natural vegetation enrichment. In peatlands includes revegetation of Shorea balangeran, Dyera costulata, and endemic peat swamp species.
karbon.mitigasi3Deskripsi: Implementation of sustainable forest management practices such as Reduced Impact Logging (RIL), intensive silviculture (SILIN), and harvest rotation management to maintain forest productivity and carbon stocks. Requires FSC or PEFC certification in commercial areas.
karbon.mitigasi4Deskripsi: Restoration of hydrological functions through rewetting, canal closure, canal blocking construction, and water management to maintain peat moisture and suppress carbon emissions and fire risk. Based on the Peatland Rewetting and Conservation (PRC) approach.
karbon.mitigasi5Deskripsi: Periodic monitoring of peat groundwater table levels using piezometers, automatic water level loggers, or monitoring wells to ensure peat remains moist according to restoration targets. TMAT target: ≤ 40 cm from peat surface per BRG/BRGM Indonesia regulation.
karbon.mitigasi6Deskripsi: Development of plantation forests, agroforestry, enrichment planting (ENR), and vegetation conservation to increase biomass and long-term carbon sequestration. In peatlands, includes planting of native peat tree species (Calophyllum, Pandanus, Syzygium).
karbon.mitigasi7Judul: Forest & Land Fire Prevention and Control (Karhutla)
karbon.mitigasi7Deskripsi: Routine patrols, integrated early warning systems (LAPAN, BMKG, FIRMS NASA), construction of firebreaks, peat water management, training of Community Fire Care (MPA) groups, provision of firefighting equipment, and emergency response plans (Fire Management Plan).
karbon.mitigasi8Deskripsi: Protection of wildlife habitats and endemic species (orangutans, proboscis monkeys, arowana fish, false gharial) to maintain ecosystem balance. Uses CCB (Climate, Community & Biodiversity Standards) as the co-benefits framework.
karbon.mitigasi8Kpi2: Number of key species individuals (camera trap)
karbon.mitigasi9Deskripsi: Carbon stock measurement based on Permanent Sample Plots (PSP), land cover change monitoring using multispectral satellite imagery (Sentinel-2, Landsat), LiDAR, drones, and periodic field inventories. Reporting in accordance with Verra VCS standards with accredited third-party verification (Validation and Verification Body / VVB).
karbon.mitigasi10Deskripsi: Measurement of CO₂ and CH₄ emissions from peat surfaces using closed dynamic chambers, eddy covariance towers, and TMAT-based emission models. Use of Tier 2/Tier 3 IPCC emission factors for tropical peatlands.
karbon.mitigasi11Deskripsi: Integration of mangrove and coastal swamp ecosystems into total carbon stock calculations, if the project area borders coastal areas or large river estuaries.
karbon.adaptasiDesc: Enhancement of social, economic, and ecological resilience through 9 adaptation and empowerment activities
karbon.adaptasi1Deskripsi: Strengthening community capacity through training, environmental education, increasing the role of women and youth, village institutional development, and fulfillment of Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) rights of indigenous communities.
karbon.adaptasi2Deskripsi: Livelihood diversification through non-timber forest products (NTFP) such as honey (Trigona and Apis), rattan, purun, medicinal plants, swamp fisheries (arowana, climbing perch), ecotourism, and Payment for Ecosystem Services (PES)-based enterprises.
karbon.adaptasi3Deskripsi: Integration of forestry plants (rubber, tengkawang, jelutung) and agriculture (rice, local horticulture) to increase land productivity without forest conversion. In peatlands: paludiculture development (wetland-based agriculture) with sago, purun, and jelutung species.
karbon.adaptasi4Deskripsi: Development of biomass energy, communal biogas, village-scale solar panels, watershed-based clean water management, wildlife crossings, and infrastructure adaptive to floods and drought.
karbon.adaptasi5Deskripsi: Development of Long-Term Forest Management Plans (RPHJP), strengthening of village regulations (village forest protection regulations), establishment of area management groups, and increased transparency of carbon project management through open reporting systems.
karbon.adaptasi6Deskripsi: Structured cooperation between central and regional governments, indigenous communities, the private sector (carbon off-takers), academia, conservation NGOs, and international institutions (UNDP, World Bank, GEF, GCF) to support long-term project sustainability.
karbon.adaptasi7Judul: Participation in International Carbon Markets and Standards
karbon.adaptasi7Deskripsi: Project development in accordance with Verra VCS, CCB, CORSIA (aviation), and national carbon trading mechanisms (Indonesia Carbon Exchange / IDXCarbon, SPEI) as well as international ones (bilateral Article 6.2 and multilateral Article 6.4 UNFCCC).
karbon.adaptasi8Deskripsi: Development of local food systems based on forest ecosystems (forest-based food systems): cultivation of local fish, utilization of forest foods (tubers, forest fruits, honey), and local seed banks for adaptation to climate change.
karbon.adaptasi9Deskripsi: Climate education programs for schools, village youth, and environmental cadres: locally contextual climate change materials, participatory mapping, and community-based environmental monitoring training.

hhbk.h1Line2: NTFP: Natural Wealth That Keeps Forests Standing.
hhbk.tagline: From 183 thousand hectares of sustainable forest, we harvest life — without cutting down a single tree.
hhbk.apaItuP1: Non-Timber Forest Products (NTFP) are all biological and non-biological products originating from forests, other than logs and processed timber. In Indonesian regulation, NTFP is recognized in Law No. 41 of 1999 on Forestry and more technically in Government Regulation No. 35 of 2002.
hhbk.apaItuP2: In Social Forestry areas managed by communities together with YAMAL, NTFP has become the backbone of the local economy — from Gunung Mas rattan to Katingan peatland purun.
hhbk.point1Desc: NTFP harvesting does not require tree felling — forests remain standing and functioning.
hhbk.point2Desc: A single forest area produces multiple commodities simultaneously — creating income diversification.
hhbk.point3Desc: Direct economic benefits to Social Forestry permit holders — indigenous and local communities.
hhbk.point4Desc: NTFP areas are also REDD+ project candidates — supporting climate change mitigation.

hhbk.mineralNarrative: The highland mineral forests of Gunung Mas and upper Kapuas are Kalimantan's warehouse of premium commodities. Here, rattan vines climb through the canopy, agarwood forms from tree wounds healing into gold, and wild honey drips from bee nests in the highest branches.
hhbk.gambutTitle: Peat Swamp Forest — Katingan, Kapuas, Pulang Pisau (~94,000 ha)
hhbk.gambutNarrative: Central Kalimantan's peat forests are among the richest carbon ecosystems on Earth. Across Kapuas, Katingan, and Pulang Pisau, communities harvest purun, tap jelutung latex, and fish from natural canals connecting village to village.
hhbk.produkPerikananDesc: Beyond forest products, Central Kalimantan's peatland ecosystems also hold fishery potential sustainably managed by SF communities
hhbk.perikanan1Desc: Central Kalimantan's peat ecosystems are rich in local fish species such as snakehead, giant snakehead, climbing perch, three-spot gourami, and dwarf snakehead. SF communities manage fisheries sustainably as a source of food and income.
hhbk.perikanan2Desc: Development of aquaculture in peatland areas with environmentally friendly systems — utilizing canals and natural ponds without damaging peatland ecosystems.
hhbk.perikanan3Desc: Processing fishery yields into value-added products — smoked fish, dried fish, fish floss, fish crackers, and traditional Dayak fermented products.

hhbk.pemasaran2Desc: Building distribution channels from village to city — through digital platforms, retail partnerships, exhibitions, and direct-to-consumer to expand market access.

apiEsg.heading2: Program Data Access for ESG Partners
apiEsg.heroDescription: YAMAL provides an API Licence to access verified data from <1>Carbon Project</1>, <1>NTFP</1>, and <1>Research & Development</1> — covering 91 Social Forestry Groups across 183,531 hectares in Central Kalimantan.
apiEsg.tigaPilarApi: Three Pillars of API Data Sources

apiEsg.cat2Desc: Biodiversity information from Social Forestry areas — flora and fauna species, IUCN conservation status, biodiversity index, and critical habitat area protected. Data from camera trap, line transect, and point count monitoring.

apiEsg.feature2Desc: Data is available in JSON/RESTful API format compatible with corporate ESG systems
apiEsg.feature3Desc: Data is updated periodically based on field monitoring results and MRV verification

berita.featuredExcerpt: Yayasan Antangpatahu Mahaga Lewu (Yayasan AMAL) marked a historic milestone with the signing of a Cooperation Agreement (PKS) with two SF groups — LPHD Tambak Bajai (Kapuas) and LPHD Gohong (Pulang Pisau) — at Hotel Best Western, Palangka Raya, on Wednesday (27/8/2025).
berita.featuredContent:
**Palangka Raya** – Yayasan Antangpatahu Mahaga Lewu (Yayasan AMAL) officially marked a historic milestone in its presence in Central Kalimantan by signing a Cooperation Agreement (PKS) with two Social Forestry (PS) groups on Wednesday (27/8/2025). The event, held at Hotel Best Western in Palangka Raya, was attended by representatives from the Ministry of Forestry of the Republic of Indonesia, the Head of the Banjarbaru Social Forestry Center, and the Central Kalimantan Provincial Forestry Office.

The cooperation covers activities in environmental services (**Non-Extractive Compensation**/NEK) and the development of Non-Timber Forest Products (NTFPs) in Social Forestry forest areas. However, the parties did not publicly disclose the operational clauses of the agreement, adhering to principles of legal compliance and partnership confidentiality.

The signing was carried out symbolically by the leadership of Yayasan AMAL with two Village Forest Management Institutions (LPHD): **LPHD Tambak Bajai** representing Kapuas Regency, and **LPHD Gohong** representing Pulang Pisau Regency. Both groups are considered to represent the ecological potential and institutional maturity of Social Forestry in their respective regions.

**Government Representatives Appreciate the Collaboration**

The Head of the Banjarbaru Social Forestry Center, **E. Nopriadi, S.Hut., M.T.**, who attended the event, stated that this partnership model between a non-profit foundation and Social Forestry groups aligns with national policy. **"The government fully supports synergy that prioritizes forest conservation while improving the welfare of forest village communities,"** he said.

Meanwhile, a representative of the Directorate General of Social Forestry at the Ministry of Forestry expressed hope that this collaboration could serve as an example for other regions in managing Social Forestry areas productively and equitably.

The Central Kalimantan Provincial Forestry Office, represented by its Head, **Agustan Saining, S.Hut., M.Si.**, also conveyed its commitment to oversee and facilitate the implementation of the agreement on the ground.

**Yayasan AMAL's Commitment: Improving the Livelihoods of PS Groups**

The Chairman of Yayasan Antangpatahu Mahaga Lewu, **Ir. Apep Yusup**, told reporters after the event that this signing is a tangible manifestation of the foundation's support for small-scale forest managers. **"We stand to assist, not to take over. This is a historic milestone for us in Central Kalimantan. Our focus is to improve the livelihoods of Social Forestry groups through mentoring, responsible financing access, and the development of environmental services and NTFPs,"** he said.

The LPHD chairpersons who attended also appreciated the negotiation process, which was considered participatory and transparent. They expressed hope that this cooperation would encourage village economic independence without compromising the ecological functions of the forest.

This signing also marks Yayasan AMAL's first step after officially obtaining legal entity status in mid-2025. The implementation of the agreement is planned to begin after socialization to PS group members in each village.

news.article8Title: Yayasan Antangpatahu Mahaga Lewu Signs Agreement with Two Social Forestry Groups, Officially Begins Work in Central Kalimantan
news.article8Excerpt: A historic milestone for Social Forestry in Central Kalimantan: Yayasan AMAL officially signed cooperation agreements with two LPHDs — Tambak Bajai (Kapuas) and Gohong (Pulang Pisau) — on August 27, 2025 in Palangka Raya, witnessed by the Ministry of Forestry and Central Kalimantan Forestry Agency.
news.article8Content:
Palangka Raya – Yayasan Antangpatahu Mahaga Lewu (Yayasan AMAL) resmi menandai tonggak sejarah keberadaannya di Kalimantan Tengah dengan melakukan penandatanganan Perjanjian Kerja Sama (PKS) bersama dua kelompok Perhutanan Sosial (PS), Rabu (27/8/2025). Acara yang berlangsung di Hotel Best Western, Palangka Raya itu dihadiri oleh perwakilan Kementerian Kehutanan RI, Kepala Balai Perhutanan Sosial Banjarbaru, serta Dinas Kehutanan Provinsi Kalimantan Tengah.

Kerja sama tersebut mencakup kegiatan di bidang jasa lingkungan (Non-Extractive Compensation/NEK) serta pengembangan Hasil Hutan Bukan Kayu (HHBK) di kawasan hutan Perhutanan Sosial. Namun, para pihak tidak merincikan klausul operasional perjanjian secara terbuka, dengan tetap berpegang pada prinsip kepatuhan hukum dan kerahasiaan kemitraan.

Penandatanganan dilakukan secara simbolis oleh pimpinan Yayasan AMAL dengan dua Lembaga Pengelola Hutan Desa (LPHD), yakni LPHD Tambak Bajai yang mewakili Kabupaten Kapuas, dan LPHD Gohong yang mewakili Kabupaten Pulang Pisau. Kedua kelompok ini dipandang mewakili potensi ekologis dan kematangan kelembagaan Perhutanan Sosial di wilayah masing-masing.

**Perwakilan Pemerintah Apresiasi Kolaborasi**

Kepala Balai Perhutanan Sosial Banjarbaru, E. Nopriadi, S.Hut., M.T., yang turut hadir menyatakan bahwa model kemitraan antara yayasan nirlaba dan kelompok Perhutanan Sosial seperti ini sejalan dengan kebijakan nasional. “Pemerintah mendukung penuh sinergi yang mengedepankan aspek kelestarian hutan sekaligus peningkatan kesejahteraan masyarakat desa hutan,” ujarnya.

Sementara itu, perwakilan Direktorat Jenderal Perhutanan Sosial Kementerian Kehutanan RI dalam sambutannya berharap agar kolaborasi ini dapat menjadi contoh bagi daerah lain dalam mengelola kawasan Perhutanan Sosial secara produktif dan berkeadilan.

Dinas Kehutanan Provinsi Kalimantan Tengah yang diwakili oleh Kepala Dinas, Agustan Saining, S.Hut., M.Si., juga menyampaikan komitmennya untuk mengawal dan memfasilitasi pelaksanaan perjanjian tersebut di lapangan.

**Komitmen Yayasan AMAL: Tingkatkan Harkat Hidup PS**

Ketua Yayasan Antangpatahu Mahaga Lewu, Ir. Apep Yusup, kepada awak media usai acara menyebutkan bahwa penandatanganan ini merupakan wujud nyata keberpihakan yayasan kepada masyarakat pengelola hutan skala kecil. “Kami berdiri untuk mendampingi, bukan mengambil alih. Ini tonggak sejarah kami di Kalimantan Tengah. Fokus kami adalah meningkatkan harkat hidup kelompok Perhutanan Sosial melalui pendampingan, akses pembiayaan yang bertanggung jawab, dan pengembangan jasa lingkungan serta HHBK,” katanya.

Para ketua LPHD yang hadir juga mengapresiasi proses negosiasi yang dinilai partisipatif dan transparan. Mereka berharap kerja sama ini mampu mendorong kemandirian ekonomi desa tanpa mengorbankan fungsi ekologis hutan.

Penandatanganan ini sekaligus menjadi langkah perdana Yayasan AMAL setelah resmi berbadan hukum pada pertengahan tahun 2025. Rencananya, implementasi perjanjian akan dimulai setelah sosialisasi kepada anggota kelompok PS di masing-masing desa. (***)
news.article2Title: Taiwan-Indonesia High-Integrity Nature-Based Solutions Cooperation Framework Summit Successfully Held
news.article2Excerpt: Asia Assets Developments Foundation (AADi) together with Yayasan Antangpatahu Mahaga Lewu and Semuda Indonesia Timur successfully held the Taiwan-Indonesia Cooperation Summit in Jakarta on April 10, 2026. A total of 150 guests attended and 5 flagship high-quality carbon projects were launched.
news.article2Content:
Indonesia is the world's third-largest archipelagic nation, with the greatest potential for mangrove forest development globally. However, international carbon markets often lack high-quality projects that are credible, verified, and scalable. To address this challenge, five high-quality products were officially launched.

**Asia Assets Developments Foundation (AADi)** hosted the **"Taiwan-Indonesia High-Integrity Nature-Based Solutions Cooperation Framework Summit"** on April 10 in Jakarta. Yayasan Antangpatahu Mahaga Lewu, Semuda Indonesia Timur, and several strategic partners collaborated to promote environmental conservation, carbon management, and sustainable development.

A total of **150 invited guests** from both countries attended, including government representatives, academics, business actors, and environmental NGOs.

Through this meeting, both parties reached several important agreements:

**1. Establishing a high-integrity nature-based solutions cooperation framework** — Utilizing advanced MRV (Monitoring, Reporting, Verification) technology to ensure every ton of carbon credits generated is traceable, verified, and meets international standards such as CCB, Plan Vivo, and SD VISta.

**2. Launch of 5 flagship projects** — Including restoration of 2,750 hectares of mangrove forests in East Kalimantan, orangutan habitat protection, and Dayak community-based economic development. These projects are expected to generate 1 million tons of high-quality carbon credits per year over the next 10 years.

**3. Establishment of the "Taiwan-Indonesia Blue Carbon Innovation Center"** — This center will serve as a research, training, and incubation hub for blue carbon technology in Southeast Asia.

**4. Memorandum of Understanding (MOU)** — Signed between AADi, Yayasan Antangpatahu Mahaga Lewu, and several Taiwanese universities. The cooperation includes technology exchange, research scholarships, and community development.

The Taiwanese side stated that Taiwan's experience in environmental technology and ecological restoration can help Indonesia achieve its NDC targets. Meanwhile, the Indonesian side welcomed green investments that involve indigenous communities and preserve Dayak local wisdom.
news.article3Title: Yayasan AMAL Holds FGD with Central Kalimantan Provincial Government, UPT KPHL Kapuas Kahayan Presents Cooperation Achievements
news.article3Excerpt: Yayasan AMAL held a Socialization and FGD with the Central Kalimantan Provincial Government at Hotel Luwansa, Palangka Raya. The Head of UPT KPHL Kapuas Kahayan presented the progress of the ongoing PKS, and UPT Heads agreed to invite the expansion of assistance to other regions in Central Kalimantan.
news.article3Content:
**Palangka Raya** – Yayasan Antang Patahu Mahaga Lewu (Yayasan AMAL) held a Socialization and Forum Group Discussion (FGD) with the Central Kalimantan Provincial Government on Thursday (22/1/2026). Taking place at Hotel Luwansa, Palangka Raya, this event served as a strategic coordination forum between the foundation, regional government, and forestry technical units across Central Kalimantan.

The FGD was attended by the Head of the Central Kalimantan Provincial Forestry Office, representatives from the Social Forestry Center Region II Mr. **Benny Tomasila**, and all Heads of UPT KPHP (Production Forest Management Unit) and KPHL (Protection Forest Management Unit) across the province.

**Foundation Presentation and Government Support**

The Chairman of Yayasan Antang Patahu Mahaga Lewu, **Ir. Apep Yusup**, in his remarks conveyed that the foundation's presence in Central Kalimantan aims to assist Social Forestry (PS) groups in technical aspects, institutional capacity, and responsible capital access. He also presented the ongoing assistance programs, particularly in the foundation's initial focus areas.

**"We are committed to synergizing with regional government and technical units. This FGD is important so that directives from the Forestry Office and the Social Forestry Center become our foundation in developing future work plans,"** said Ir. Apep Yusup.

The Head of the Central Kalimantan Provincial Forestry Office, **Agustan Saining, S.Hut., M.Si.**, appreciated the foundation's initiative and stated that the provincial government opens the widest possible space for development partners with good track records.

**Presentation by Head of UPT KPHL Kapuas Kahayan: PKS Cooperation Already Underway**

One of the key sessions in the FGD was the presentation by **Mr. Miko Duwiter, S.Hut., M.Si.**, as Head of UPT KPHL Kapuas Kahayan. He reported that in his working area, **a Cooperation Agreement (PKS) has already been established** between Yayasan Antang Patahu Mahaga Lewu and local Social Forestry groups.

Without disclosing the detailed operational clauses of the agreement, Miko Duwiter explained that the cooperation includes assistance in Non-Timber Forest Product (NTFP) management and environmental services development. According to him, the foundation's presence has had a positive impact on the institutional capacity of PS groups in the KPHL Kapuas Kahayan area.

**"We see Yayasan AMAL as a partner that genuinely assists the community. The PKS that has been running quite well and we hope this collaboration can continue and be expanded to other areas,"** said Miko Duwiter in his presentation.

The statement received positive responses from other UPT Heads. Several expressed interest in establishing similar cooperation in their respective areas.

**FGD Results: Expansion of Cooperation to Other Areas**

Currently, Yayasan AMAL is actively assisting PS groups in four areas: UPT KPHL Kapuas Kahayan, KPHP Katingan Hilir, KPHP Kahayan Hulu, and KPHP Kahayan Hilir.

The attending UPT Heads agreed to invite Yayasan AMAL to expand the scope of assistance to other areas in Central Kalimantan. The representative of the Social Forestry Center Region II, **Benny Tomasila**, expressed full support for the expansion plan, while prioritizing technical coordination with the center and the forestry office.

**Closing**

The FGD activity concluded with a group photo session and friendly gathering. Yayasan AMAL committed to following up on invitations from UPT Heads through field visits and the preparation of locally specific cooperation frameworks. The Central Kalimantan Provincial Forestry Office will serve as the primary facilitator.

With the successful convening of this FGD, the synergy between regional government, forestry technical units, and civil society organizations is expected to grow stronger, for the success of sustainable Social Forestry programs in Central Kalimantan.

privacy.heroDesc: We value your privacy. This page explains how Yayasan AMAL collects, uses, and protects your personal information.
privacy.section1Desc: Yayasan AMAL may collect personal information that you voluntarily provide, including but not limited to:
privacy.section1Item1: Full name and email address when filling out contact or, forms
privacy.section1Item2: Phone number and address when registering as a partner or donor
privacy.section1Item3: Payment information processed through secure third-party payment gateways
privacy.section1Item4: Website usage data through cookies and Google Analytics (pages visited, visit duration, browser used)
privacy.section1Item5: Organization information and position when submitting partnership applications
privacy.section2Desc: The information we collect is used for the following purposes:
privacy.section2Item1: Processing, and sending confirmations and fund usage reports
privacy.section2Item2: Responding to inquiries, information requests, and partnership applications
privacy.section2Item3: Sending newsletters, program reports, and activity information (you may unsubscribe at any time)
privacy.section2Item4: Improving website quality and user experience through anonymous data analysis
privacy.section2Item5: Fulfilling legal obligations and reporting to relevant authorities
privacy.section3Desc: We implement security measures to protect your personal information:
privacy.section3Item1: SSL (Secure Socket Layer) encryption for all sensitive data transmissions
privacy.section3Item2: Restricted access to personal data — only authorized and trained staff
privacy.section3Item3: Data stored on secure servers with firewalls and 24/7 monitoring
privacy.section3Item4: Data retention as needed — data is deleted when no longer needed for collection purposes
privacy.section3Item5: No credit/debit card data stored — all payments processed by third-party gateways
privacy.section4Desc: Our website uses cookies and similar tracking technologies to:
privacy.section4Item1: Google Analytics — anonymously analyze website traffic (does not identify individuals)
privacy.section4Item2: Session cookies — maintain user sessions while browsing (automatically deleted when browser is closed)
privacy.section4Item3: Preference cookies — remember your language preferences
privacy.section4Note: You can disable cookies through your browser settings. However, some website features may not function optimally.
privacy.section5Desc: Yayasan AMAL does NOT sell, rent, or trade your personal information. We only share data under the following conditions:
privacy.section5Item1: With service providers (payment gateway, email service) bound by confidentiality agreements
privacy.section5Item2: If required by law, regulation, or valid legal process
privacy.section5Item3: With your explicit consent for specific purposes
privacy.section6Desc: In accordance with applicable data protection regulations, you have the right to:
privacy.section6Item1: Access the personal data we hold about you
privacy.section6Item2: Request correction of inaccurate or incomplete data
privacy.section6Item3: Request deletion of your personal data ("right to be forgotten")
privacy.section6Item4: Withdraw consent for data processing at any time
privacy.section6Item5: Object to data processing for specific purposes
privacy.section7Desc: We are committed to protecting your data. However, please be aware that no method of internet transmission or electronic storage is 100% secure. We continuously update security protocols according to the latest industry standards.
